subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured credential-shaped `skills.entries.<skill>.env` keys be admitted for intended active-skill host exec, and what scoping prevents unrelated exec children from inheriting those secrets?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible and contradicts documented host-run skill env behavior, but the fix intentionally changes how secrets reach subprocess environments and overlaps an open inverse secret-leak mitigation.

options.title: Admit scoped active-skill env secrets
options.body: Permit only explicitly configured keys for the intended active skill path, keep dangerous host env names blocked, and add tests for intended delivery plus unrelated exec stripping.

options.title: Keep metadata-only sensitive allowlist
options.body: Require each skill to declare credential-shaped env names in metadata and update docs or doctor guidance so arbitrary sensitive `skills.entries.*.env` names are not promised.

options.title: Defer to a new secret contract
options.body: Leave the sanitizer unchanged until maintainers define a SecretRef or plugin-owned credential path for CLI skills that need headless auth.

recommendation.title: Admit scoped active-skill env secrets
recommendation.body: Permit only explicitly configured keys for the intended active skill path, keep dangerous host env names blocked, and add tests for intended delivery plus unrelated exec stripping.

likelyOwner.reason: Current source blame and recent related skill-env history make Vincent Koc the best available routing owner for the security-boundary decision.
